articleTitle: IEE Colloquium on 'Transmission of HDTV by Satellite' (Digest No.092)
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Transmission of HDTV by Satellite
IEE Colloquium on Transmission of HDTV by Satellite
abstract: The author deals with three main topics: the history of the development of high definition television (HDTV) and HDTV standards to date; the main European institutions involved in HDTV; and the possible strategy for introducing HDTV services in Europe.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Transmission of HDTV by Satellite
abstract: The author discusses the issues surrounding the wideband HDTV transmission at frequencies around 22GHz. Among the topics covered are: HDMAC satellite TV transmission, receiver dishes for home reception, 12GHz TWTAs (travelling wave tube amplifiers) working at 240W, hybrid approach in transmitting digital enhancement information to accompany an HDMAC signal, HDMAC sub-Nyquist sampling process and the effects on spectrum requirements and link budget.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Transmission of HDTV by Satellite
abstract: The author describes the evolution of HD-MAC transmissions which are received by top-of-the-range TV sets with ND-MAC (normal definition-multiplexed analogue component) features. Among the topics discussed are: compatibility between present and future ND-MAC and HD-MAC services, HD-MAC receiver-decoders and HD-MAC receiver systems for the HDTV coverage of 1992 Olympic Winter Games.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Transmission of HDTV by Satellite
abstract: The authors describe the development of HDMAC which is carried out by a consortium of European companies under the EUREKA 95 project. There are twelve project groups covering every aspect of the system from the camera to the domestic receiver. Among the topics covered are: bandwidth reduction encoding, HDMAC vision signal video characteristics, transmission path Nyquist channel, HDMAC noise performance and HDMAC modulation parameters.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Transmission of HDTV by Satellite
abstract: The author describes that the use of digital modulation for HDTV broadcasting reduces the protection-ratio requirement sufficiently to permit common-frequency operation. This enables more programmes to be broadcast to each country within a given band, compared with the use of analogue modulation, while offering greater flexibility for development.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
